question: Which of the following was a major long-term socioeconomic impact of the Dutch commercial presence on the Coromandel coast during the 17th century?
options: Complete replacement of the traditional barter system in rural areas with Dutch copper coins.
Integration of local weavers into a global commercial market through the advance-payment (dadan) system, increasing their dependency on merchant capital.
The absolute decline of traditional Indian merchant guilds due to Dutch monopoly laws.
A mass migration of South Indian weavers to Batavia and Amsterdam.
explanation: The Dutch VOC relied on the dadan (advance-payment) system, where merchant-brokers gave advances to weavers to purchase raw materials and sustain themselves while producing specific textiles. While this initially stimulated production, it integrated local artisans into a volatile global market and reduced their independence, making them dependent on the merchant-brokers and European company capital.
